newsitem.title: USA: GT Bicycles sees Q2 earnings shortfall.
newsitem.headline: GT Bicycles sees Q2 earnings shortfall.

text.p: GT Bicycles Inc, a maker of premium bicycles, Thursday warned that second quarter earnings will not meet analysts' expectations.

In a statement, GT said it expects sales of about $51 million in the quarter with net income ranging from $600,000 to $800,000, or $0.06 to $0.08 per share, before a one-time relocation charge between $300,000 and $400,000.
Analysts' consensus estimate for the second quarter ended June 30 had been $0.23 a share, according to First Call.
In the year ago quarter, GT reported net income of $2.2 million, or $0.22 per share, on sales of $44.1 million.
"The domestic adult mountain bike market continues to be challenging, and poor spring weather impacted domestic results in all of our lines of business," said Mike Haynes, chief executive officer.
Haynes added, however, international growth is solid with sales up 80 percent over the year ago period. Overseas sales now comprise about 29 percent of total company sales.
Also, the company's Harley Davidson bike has shown some early success, helping to offset shortfalls elsewhere.
GT expects to report its final second quarter results in early August.
The company's stock ended trading Thursday up 3/8 at 8-1/4. Its announcement was made after the market closed.
